subject: sum-to-one constraint on fixed effects coefs

messages.author: e5f939e8ec1198ca
messages.subject: sum-to-one constraint on fixed effects coefs
parts:
Hi all - 

We're working on an geostatistical problem using INLA with a SPDE random field. We have reason to enforce a sum-to-one constraint across our 5 fixed effects coefficients and it's unclear to me if either the 'constr' option in f() or 'cross' in control.predictor() might be used for this purpose. If this isn't easily done another option for us would be to force positive coefficients. My questions are:

1) Is it possible to impose a sum-to-1 constraint across the fixed effects coefficients and how might that be done for N fixed effects?

2) If this isn't possible, I see two possible ways to enforce positivity in the fixed effects coefs. Method one would be to use 'clinear()'. Method two would be to use a positive prior for the fixed effects. Is one of these options preferred over the other and, if so, why?

Much thanks,
Aaron

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] sum-to-one constraint on fixed effects coefs
parts:
Hi,

it's possible to use a combination of
data$covar <- 1:5
formula <- ... + f(covar, model="iid", extraconstr=list(A=matrix(1,1,5), e=1))
and
control.predictor=list(A=A)
to get such a sum-to-one constraint. The linear combination matrix A
for control.predictor is probably easiest to construct with
inla.stack().
Something like
inla.stack(data=..., A=list(cbind(cov1, cov2, cov3, cov4, cov5)),
effects=list(list(covar=1:5)))

There may also be other options; control.predictor-cross unfortunately
only does sum-to-zero.

For clinear vs. positive prior; clinear is essentially that.

Since you're using SPDEs, you likely already use inla.stack, so the
outline above is likely the easiest solution.

However, note that the sum-to-one constraint doesn't imply positivity
of the individual coefficients, so you seem to be asking two different
questions.

Finn

Hi Finn - 

Thanks for the quick reply. I hadn't realized that this was available and it's quite exciting for us! 

I tried implementing this on a test example but I'm a bit confused about a few things in building the stack(s) correctly. 

To be clearer, I already have a inla.stack() object I was using to fit the SPDE models. I believe that I should be leaving that stack untouched, building a second stack pertaining to the covariate-constraint (cc), and then using inla.stack()  to combine the data and cc stack. So far so good?

Assuming that's the suggestion here, let me ask a few more detailed questions about the cc-stack:

1) I have a dataset, data,  with n_d rows and I have n_c covariates. If I simply set data$covar=1:n_c it will recycle 1:n_c across the number of data points, n_d. This doesn't seem correct to me. To what data.frame should I be appending covar=1:n_c?

2) Closely tied to (1), what data information to I need to include in the cc stack? Since you suggest that the A-matrix should be comprised of the covariate column vectors, I believe that means the data vectors in the cc-stack must also be of length n_d, but that brings us back to question (1). I tried simply passing in my response as the data in the cc-stack  (as I did in the data stack), but then the model can't find 'covar' in f(covar, model="iid", extraconstr=list(A=matrix(1,1,5), e=1)) which was to be expected. So it seems like I need to pass in covar into the data in the cc-stack, but I'm unclear how the n_c-vector aligns with the n_d rows of the covariate A-matrix (A=list(cbind(cov1, cov2, cov3, cov4, ..., covN_c)).

3) Lastly, I also tried adding the column data$covar=1:n_c to my n_d long data matrix (which recycled n_c as needed to get to length n_d) and running:

inla.stack(data=list(y=data$y, covar=data$covar),  A=list(cbind(cov1, cov2, cov3, cov4, cov5)), effects=list(list(covar=1:n_c)) but then I get an error stating: 
"Names for data and effects must not coincide."

Any additional clarifications or pointers would be much appreciated.

As for your comment on the sum-to-one vs positivity in the coefs. -  I 100% agree. We're implementing a stacked ensemble type approach as suggested here: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.03278 . Realistically the sum-to-1 is what we want but the paper claims that in practice positivity on the coefs seemed to often be enough which is why I asked about it ( in case the sum-to-1 wasn't feasible).

Much thanks, Aaron

parts:
> inla.stack(data=list(y=data$y, covar=data$covar), A=list(cbind(cov1, cov2,
> cov3, cov4, cov5)), effects=list(list(covar=1:n_c)) but then I get an error

On 27 October 2017 at 03:59, Aaron OZ <zima...@gmail.com> wrote:
> To be clearer, I already have a inla.stack() object I was using to fit the
> SPDE models. I believe that I should be leaving that stack untouched,
> building a second stack pertaining to the covariate-constraint (cc), and
> then using inla.stack() to combine the data and cc stack. So far so good?
Not quite; you'll need to add to your existing inla.stack() call instead.

> 1) I have a dataset, data, with n_d rows and I have n_c covariates. If I
> simply set data$covar=1:n_c it will recycle 1:n_c across the number of data
> points, n_d. This doesn't seem correct to me. To what data.frame should I be
> appending covar=1:n_c?

No, the inla.stack-construction will take care of it instead.

If you have an inla.stack call with an spde component, e.g.

A.field <- inla.spde.make.A(...)
index.field <- inla.spde.make.index("field", ...)
stack <- inla.stack(
data=list(y=data$y),
A=list(A.field),
effects=list(index.field) )

then in order to add the effect of the covariates, you need

A.covar <- cbind(cov1, cov2, cov3, ...)
stack <- inla.stack(
data=list(y=data$y),
A=list(A.field, A.covar),
effects=list(index.field, list(covar=1:ncol(A.covar))) )

In the formula,

formula <- y ~ -1 + f(covar, model="iid",
list(A=matrix(1,1,ncol(A.covar)), e=1)) + f(field, model=field.spde)


If the above doesn't work, I'll need you to provide the precise code
and R output messages.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] sum-to-one constraint on fixed effects coefs
parts:
Recall that you also need
inla(...,
data=inla.stack.data(stack, field.spde=field.spde),
control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack)))

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] sum-to-one constraint on fixed effects coefs
parts:
Addendum:
In order to mimic the fixed, vague prior for the covariate
coefficients, you need to fix the precision parameter of the "iid"
model, so that the latent variables are effectively treated as "fixed
effects" and not "random effects". in the f() term for covar:

f(covar, model="iid",
list(A=matrix(1,1,ncol(A.covar)), e=1),
hyper=list(theta=list(
initial=log(inla.set.control.fixed.default()$prec),
fixed=TRUE)))

If you do not do this, then the precision will be estimated from the
data, but since there is only ncol(A.covar) latent variables (a small
number), that is unlikely to be very stable.

(Currently, the default fixed effect precision, from
inla.set.control.fixed.default()$prec, is 0.001)

Finn
